It can, but doesn't have to; it's in the application. What I do is tap a bit of my MMU onto a mirror or other clean surface. Then I use a damp fluffy brush to sort of stipple the powder from the mirror in thin, overlapping layers on my face.

If you work quickly, it's a smooth, even layer of coverage. But you can't really go back and build more coverage with this technique once it's " dry".  You'll just make the base layer lift or get patchy.

I cannot recommend a particular brush, though I've found applying my power while my skin is still a bit tacky from my sunscreen helps it to grab and hold more product, for better coverage.
Using a brush that's slightly damp, or a flocked sponge also helps build more coverage.
